chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

The salat of al-Maghrib and al-'Isha' at Jam' are with one adhan and two iqamahs, and do not perform anything between them. He said: And this is how the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed salat.
From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muskan, from 'Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, who said: I said to Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام:
If I perform salat al-Maghrib at Jam', should I perform the rak'ahs after al-Maghrib? He said: No. Perform al-Maghrib and al-'Isha', then perform the rak'ahs afterward.

key_terms.أَذَانٍ: the call to prayer, here performed once for both salats
key_terms.إِقَامَتَيْنِ: two iqamahs, one for each of the two salats
key_terms.بِجَمْعٍ: at Jam', meaning al-Muzdalifah, where the two salats are combined
key_terms.رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, whose practice is cited as precedent
key_terms.صَلَاةُ: the prescribed salat being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.ٱلرَّكَعَاتِ: the additional rak'ahs asked about after al-Maghrib
key_terms.ٱلْعِشَاءِ: the night salat joined with al-Maghrib at Jam'
key_terms.ٱلْمَغْرِبِ: the sunset salat combined at al-Muzdalifah

ai.seo_question: How should al-Maghrib and al-'Isha' be combined at al-Muzdalifah, and when are the extra rak'ahs performed?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the manner of combining al-Maghrib and al-'Isha' at al-Muzdalifah: with one adhan and two iqamahs, without performing anything between them. It also clarifies that the supererogatory rak'ahs after al-Maghrib are delayed until after completing both obligatory salats, in accordance with the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
